title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 212 (Investigation into affairs of Company by Serious Fraud Investigation Office)

content.overview: Section 212 empowers the Central Government to assign investigation into the affairs of a company to the Serious Fraud Investigation Office on the grounds stated in the section (including on receipt of a report under s. 208, or where the Government is of opinion that investigation by SFIO is necessary). Once a case is assigned to SFIO, no other investigating agency of the Central or State Government shall proceed with investigation of an offence under the Act in respect of that case. The investigating officer has the powers of an inspector. Arrest is governed by the section, and bail in an SFIO case is restricted as provided. The investigation report is filed as the section directs. Fraud charges commonly engage section 447.
content.glance: CG assigns company investigation to SFIO on statutory grounds; exclusivity — other agencies do not proceed on the same Act offence; inspector powers; arrest and restricted bail; report as directed; often linked with s. 447 fraud.
content.study: Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary to investigate into the affairs of a company by the Serious Fraud Investigation Office, it may assign the investigation to SFIO. The assignment may follow a report under section 208 or other grounds the section states. Where a case has been assigned to SFIO, no other investigating agency of Central or State Government shall proceed with investigation in respect of any offence under the Act in that case. The investigating officer of SFIO has the powers of an inspector under the Act. Arrest and bail are governed by the special provisions in the section. Current-law framing: confirm CG assignment to SFIO; apply exclusivity against parallel agency investigation of the same Act offence; note inspector powers, arrest and bail rules; link to s. 447 where fraud is alleged. Distinct from general CG investigation under s. 210 and from Tribunal-ordered investigation under s. 213.

sections.heading: Assignment
sections.body: Central Government may assign investigation of a company’s affairs to SFIO on the grounds in the section.

sections.heading: Exclusivity
sections.body: Once assigned, no other Central or State investigating agency proceeds with investigation of an offence under the Act in respect of that case.

sections.heading: Powers, Arrest and Bail
sections.body: Investigating officer has powers of an inspector; arrest governed by the section; bail restricted as provided.

sections.heading: Report and Fraud
sections.body: Investigation report filed as the section directs; fraud allegations commonly engage section 447.

provisions.title: Investigation into affairs of Company by Serious Fraud Investigation Office

examples.title: Exclusivity after assignment
examples.body: CG assigns investigation of Company X to SFIO under s. 212. A State police unit then seeks to continue a parallel investigation of the same Companies Act offence. Section 212’s exclusivity rule bars that parallel proceeding on the Act offence in that case.

examples.title: Arrest and bail
examples.body: An SFIO investigating officer arrests a person in connection with a s. 212 investigation. Bail is governed by the special restrictions in the section, not only by general criminal procedure.

hypotheticals.question: Can SFIO start investigating a company on its own without Central Government assignment?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 212 contemplates assignment by the Central Government of investigation into the affairs of a company to SFIO. The institutional existence of SFIO under s. 211 does not by itself authorise investigation of a named company without the assignment process.

distinctions.title: SFIO investigation (s. 212) vs CG inspector investigation (s. 210)
distinctions.left: Assignment to SFIO; exclusivity; special arrest/bail rules
distinctions.right: CG appoints inspectors on four triggers; general investigation route

misconceptions.trap: Any police station can continue a Companies Act fraud case after SFIO assignment of that case.
misconceptions.correction: Once a case is assigned to SFIO under s. 212, no other Central or State investigating agency shall proceed with investigation of an offence under the Act in respect of that case.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 212 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm CG assignment to SFIO. II. Apply exclusivity. III. Note powers, arrest and bail. IV. Distinguish s. 210/213. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Assignment facts; exclusivity; arrest/bail issues; precise relief.
